same as stream, just a different interface
checks expected order, and the + indicates that element had a next sibling at time of emission

i.norm:
Appends a compact, human-readable summary of {@code element} to {@code summary}, encoding the details this test cares about for each emitted element:
  • the tag name (e.g. {@code div})
  • {@code #id} if the element has an {@code id} attribute
  • {@code [text]} if the element has its own (non-child) text
  • a trailing {@code +} if the element had a next sibling when it was emitted
Each element's summary is terminated with {@code ;}.
Iterating a StreamParser emits each Element as it is completed (children before parents). This mirrors the stream() behaviour, just exposed through the Iterator interface.
Verifies the document-order emission. The "+" markers confirm that an element already had a next sibling at the moment it was emitted (see appendSummary for the encoding).
